title: Ewe 78 — 3yo Suffolk: bottle jaw and pale membranes at grass
presentation: Three-year-old Suffolk ewe from a group of forty grazing a permanent pasture in a warm, wet August. Lagging behind the group, swelling under the jaw, and two other ewes look similar. No diarrhoea reported.

stages.title: Examine the ewe and the group
stages.briefing: BCS 1.5/5. Conjunctivae very pale (FAMACHA 5). Soft, pitting submandibular oedema. HR 96 bpm, RR 36/min, temperature 39.0°C. Faeces formed. Fleece dull, no rise. Group history: last treated with a benzimidazole eight weeks ago, set-stocked on the same field all season, two more ewes with pale membranes.
stages.prompt: Which findings point to a blood-sucking parasite rather than diarrhoeal disease?

options.label: Very pale conjunctivae with a FAMACHA score of 5
options.detail: Severe anaemia scored objectively

options.label: Soft pitting submandibular oedema
options.detail: Bottle jaw from hypoproteinaemia

options.label: Formed faeces despite severe illness
options.detail: Haemonchus sucks blood without causing scour

options.label: Warm, wet August on set-stocked permanent pasture
options.detail: The conditions for a Haemonchus challenge, not a finding in the ewe

options.label: Dull fleece with no wool rise
options.detail: Non-specific ill-thrift

stages.explanation: Anaemia with bottle jaw and normal faeces is the signature of Haemonchus contortus, and it is the absence of scour that separates it from the other parasitic gastroenteritis syndromes. FAMACHA turns "she looks pale" into a number you can act on and repeat. The grazing history is what explains the outbreak and drives the plan, but it is epidemiology rather than clinical evidence.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: You are on farm with the flock gathered and can sample individuals or the group.

options.label: Faecal egg count on this ewe and a group pooled sample
options.detail: Quantifies the burden in the individual and the flock

options.label: Packed cell volume and total protein
options.detail: Grades the anaemia and the protein loss

options.label: Faecal egg count reduction test
options.detail: Anthelmintic resistance is the question behind the outbreak

options.label: Larval culture or PCR speciation of the eggs
options.detail: Confirms Haemonchus rather than another strongyle

options.label: FAMACHA scoring of the whole group
options.detail: Finds the others before they collapse

options.label: Liver fluke coproantigen or serology alone as the answer
options.detail: Worth checking on wet ground, but fluke does not usually give this picture in August

options.label: Blood culture
options.detail: Nothing here suggests septicaemia

stages.explanation: Two levels of question are being answered at once: what is wrong with this ewe, and why is it happening in this flock. The PCV grades her risk, the counts and speciation name the parasite, and the reduction test asks whether the wormer used eight weeks ago still works — which is the answer that changes next season rather than next week.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: PCV 12% (ref 27–45), total protein 42 g/L (ref 60–79), albumin 18 g/L. Faecal egg count 3,800 epg strongyle-type; pooled group count 1,900 epg. Larval speciation: 92% Haemonchus contortus. Faecal egg count reduction after benzimidazole 41% (resistance if <95%). Liver fluke coproantigen negative. Faeces formed throughout.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Haemonchosis with severe anaemia and protein loss
options.detail: PCV 12%, low albumin, 3,800 epg Haemonchus

options.label: Benzimidazole resistance on this farm
options.detail: A 41% reduction, far below the 95% threshold

options.label: The whole group is carrying a high burden
options.detail: Pooled count 1,900 epg

options.label: Liver fluke is excluded as the main cause
options.detail: Coproantigen negative

options.label: Nutritional anaemia from copper or cobalt deficiency
options.detail: Would not produce a count of 3,800 epg or bottle jaw

options.label: Coccidiosis is the flock problem
options.detail: Wrong age group, and the faeces are formed

stages.explanation: The clinical diagnosis and the farm diagnosis both land here. A 41% reduction means the wormer that was used did almost nothing, so the group has effectively been untreated for eight weeks on contaminated ground — and prescribing the same product again would repeat that. Excluding fluke matters because the two are treated with entirely different drugs.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: PCV 12%, total protein 42 g/L, 3,800 epg of which 92% Haemonchus, group count 1,900 epg, benzimidazole reduction 41%, fluke negative.

options.label: Haemonchosis on a farm with benzimidazole-resistant worms
options.detail: The parasite and the reason it is uncontrolled

options.label: Chronic fasciolosis
options.detail: Coproantigen negative and the season does not fit

options.label: Copper deficiency
options.detail: Does not cause bottle jaw or a high egg count

options.label: Coccidiosis
options.detail: A disease of lambs, with scour

options.label: Johne’s disease
options.detail: Chronic wasting with diarrhoea and normal PCV, not acute anaemia

stages.explanation: The resistance finding is what makes this diagnosis useful: this ewe needs an effective anthelmintic from a different group plus supportive care, the group needs FAMACHA screening and targeted treatment, and the farm needs a grazing and quarantine plan. A diagnosis of "worms" without the resistance half of the sentence would leave the flock exactly where it started.
